questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A friend of mine is studying at the same university and he highly recommended it and it was always a dream for me to go to Australia to explore the culture and nature and I wanted to go to an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my exchange semester, it was cool to explore a new university and a new academic culture, and meeting international students which allowed me to learn a lot. It was fun to explore new courses, which gave me the opportunity to widen my academic horizon. And this country is truly amazing, the culture, the weather, the nature, the food. And it was also nice to escape the danish winter and change it to summer.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I feel like I always was able to get the information I needed, wither by asking my host university, or reading the fact sheets from my host university. I also had a student guidance counselling at KU to get all the information I needed. For the visa and flights I did my own research.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was always able to email my host university ( the response was super fast like within a day) or at KU ( which took a little longer, about a week).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very well organised, I could tell that they put a lot of effort into it. I got all the information I needed. It was nice to meet the other international students, they did games, a campus tour and a lot of uni clubs introduced themselves ( like over 80 ) so it was nice to meet like-minded people.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky I have a friend who lives in Sydney so I could live there. Generally, fining housing is rather difficult and expansive, especially in the popular suburbs like Bondi. I choose Bondi because of the beach location, but It also took me around an hour to go to uni by bus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend coming here first and staying in a hostel and look for housing here. I know some people who were able to find housing from Europe, so online, but there are also some scammers. I personally did not want to stay at campus, it's not for me, also it was quite hard because the majority of housing was for 53 weeks and I am only here for 6 months so it was simply not possible. I know some people who live on campus mainly because their home university got a spot for them, and it was also fun and nice to meet people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Like I said I am not a student housing person, and It also was not suitable for my duration of stay.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would say fairly easy, I think the program they are using is a little old school, and they are using codes for the course but if you take time and read all the fact sheets it is pretty straight forward. I just asked the study counselling at UNSW with any question and I always got a quick reply.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When I remember correctly ( it has been a while ) I first applied at KU to be chosen for exchange and my two priorities were UNSW and USYD, in early December I got the notification that I was granted a spot from KU, I think in April I got an email from UNSW that I was chosen, and that I can login to Endeavour, their exchange program, which had a step by step guide and status with deadlines. I had to apply for pre-approval for possible courses at the faculties and I then send it for pre-approval for KU. I got my official Certificate of Enrolment in early June, with allowed me to apply for my student visa, my visa got approved a week later and then I booked my flights. All in all I am very happy with the process, there were some up and downs, especially when I had to chose the courses, because some were canceled, but if you are the fact sheet its pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: With any question I just emailed UNSW and someone from the Europe exchange team helped me pretty fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One course in the winter term was cancelled which was about the Sydney Opera house, which was sad because I know its danish design. For the winter term there were only 3 or 4 courses available for master level, and one was Australian las which is not really my area, but I ended up in Future Leader lab, which was hoarsely such a fun and informative course, one of the best courses I had! I was able to get into all the other courses I wanted, the only thing was time-management, because the courses were located at different campuses, so I had to choose based on the times. I can recommend looking easy because the seminar time are booked very fast and then you are only left with time slots in the evening.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Like it is very straightforward forward. I think I got the CoE quite late, so I could only apple for my visa vera late and the flights were pretty expansive. For the courses, the ones in the winter/ summer term are pretty limited, but its actual just exchange students or students who need extra ETCS take those courses, some students at UNSW did not even knew about the winter term. I would recommend being flexible with the courses, maybe choose 4 or 5 because of possible overlays with other courses, but I was bale to get in all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked my courses, the classes were diversified, it was a mix of lectures, seminars with group work and presentations. I liked that I had 3 submissions throughout the semester in contrast to having 1 big one at the end of the semester.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was okay, 3 courses were a good load for the semester. The assignments are quite a lot, so you are never bored thats for sure. My grades were pretty good and I defiantly learnt something new, especially during the course Future Leader Lab and Graphic Design and Society.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it was quite similar. The teaching language was English, it was a mix of lectures and seminars and group work as well as individuals projects. I like that the courses Future Leader Lab and Graphic Design and Society were quite practical with excursions and photo projects compared to the rather research based and theoretical courses I had at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Winter term: Future Leader Lab
T3: Graphic Design & Society, Social Media Campaigning, Digital Cultures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend the Future leader Lab Course. I was so much fun, the instructors put a lot of effort into it and there were a lot of excursions to firms like KPMG were we talked to sustainability officers and also to entrepreneurs focussing on sustainable leadership which was super inspiring. It was also nice because the course mainly consisted of international exchange students who all were new to Sydney so it was also nice to meet new people.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transport is quite expansive, since you cannot book a monthly plan. Alcohol and going out was also quite expansive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I would say in general life is less expansive than in Copenhagen. It is still a big international city so rent is quite high. I would say going out was more expansive than I thought. Travelling was expensive but worth it. The domestic flights in AUS are pretty cheap which was nice.I like to read and thereare multiple libraries so books were free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNSW offers a loooot of clubs but since I live quite far from campus I didn't end up going one. The people here are very active and fit and there are a lot of running clubs which I joined or pilates studios.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some events for it and also clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a club if it is convenient for you , its a good way to meet like-minded people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I did a lot of research on instagram, like must see things in Sydney. I also asked some locals about their favourite places. I would say of course the basics like the harbour bridge, the opera, Bondi beach. I further really liked the Bondi to Coogee walk, Watsons bay ( and hotel), all the parks, the botanical garden, Taronga Zoo, Darling Harbour Fireworks, try all the food its amazing,  hidden and rooftop bars, try surfing, seeing the sunset, go running at the coast. In the surrounding area the blue mountainy, Manly, Palm beach, Cronulla and the Hunter Valley.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say fairly easy, it took me a while to realise that I am not on vacation because I never lives in such a warm climate with a beach. It is harder than I thought to befriend Australians because they like to stay in their own bubble. Once I found a job I was also nice to have colleagues and ask them for places to see and it also gave me more of a routine and it was also nice to earn money and save for travelling

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and go to the events ARC ( the student association) offers. I am not the biggest party/ club going person but they had some events. Join running clubs or other sports. I also see my colleagues as friends as we are internationals so finding a job is also a good idea.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference was that they are driving on the other side of the road, I was kind of dangerous as a pedestrian. Also everything kind of closes early, the coffee shops, and clothing stores, and bars. The Australians defiantly like waking up early, at 6 everyone was out for a run, also depends on the suburb. Also, all the people are so nice.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like the active culture, and the wake-up early culture and everyone is so chilled here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared that there are a lot of international students and cultural differences.
2. There a lot of assignments.
3. Join some clubs to meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The courses are not easy, you have to work quite a bit. I was surprised that there were hardly any Australians in my class and 90 % were from China and there was quite a big language barrier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Australia is an amazing country and seeing the sun everyday defiantly contributed to my well-being. It was nice being on campus and meet your friends at the beach. It was also nice to get a job and experience the work culture. Life is pretty chilled down here, it seems like everyone is active and doing good. And traveling around was also amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say meeting new people. I am an introvert and quite sensitive to lot music so going in clubs is not my favourite. The first two weeks where you meet like 100 people and everyone is going out was a lot for me. But I also met amazing people in my courses, at running clubs, through Instagram, at work and through friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it! I am so thankful that I got the opportunity to come here for exchange. It is so cool to actual live here as a student, go to work and find a routine to really settle in and find your people. Sydney is an amazing city there is so much to do, to see and to explore. Travelling is insane, it looks like a dream. And it is a great way to broaden your academic horizon with some new courses you are interested in. And make sure you go on the winter semester so that you have summer here.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
